cells.tense: The scale in you is reading true right now, and that steadiness came out of practice, not luck.
cells.ask: Write down the one thing today you know is fair but haven't acted on. Just write it. Acting comes later, and it's yours to time.
cells.core:
The sense of what's fair is running clean right now. Not loud, not clever — it just registers. Something happens and the gut reading arrives before the reasoning does, and the reading tends to hold. That quiet instrument got made, not born, by thousands of small rehearsals most people don't bother with.

There's a sum in you that keeps the tally: what was spent against what still stands. This is the season where the tally comes back with something on it. What grew out of all that practice is ready to be picked. The practice can stop proving itself now and start feeding whatever you point it at next.
cells.sheetLine: The reading is true right now, and it was earned.
cells.verb: weighing what's right in the gut before the mind gets a vote
cells.place: a small, steady practice kept lit by repetition

cells.tense: You're running the fairness calculation ahead of events, ruling on disputes that haven't happened yet.
cells.ask: Let one decision sit unanswered until the other person actually shows up and says something. One. You don't have to promise more than that.
cells.core:
The compass is spinning ahead now, ruling on things that haven't happened. A conversation gets pre-judged before it starts, a debt tallied before it's owed. What was a clean instrument has become a reviewing chamber, and everything waits there for a verdict.

Fairness stops being fairness when it's decided in advance. The thing you're measuring hasn't been born yet and you've already filed a ruling on it. What actually steadies this is holding — the strength that contains a situation instead of settling it early. Holding without forcing returns the scale to its balance, and the tightness you feel in your practice is the settlement happening too soon.

cells.tense: You've been steering by what other people say is fair instead of by your own gut reading.
cells.ask: Say the fairness call out loud once today — to a person, not a mirror. No defending it after. Say it and let it stand where it lands.
cells.core:
The reading is still in there somewhere. When the question of what's fair comes up, the answer arrives from what other people seem to expect. The instrument didn't break. It stopped getting used.

What's running this instead is borrowed steadiness — someone else's version of the rules, doing the deciding in your place. The practice went hollow for the same reason: repetition with nothing of yours underneath it. What refills it is showing one piece of your own work to somebody, or following one instruction closely enough to finish it. The scale comes back by being used on small, real things.
cells.sheetLine: The scale is in there. It stopped getting consulted.

cells.tense: You're already acting on the fairness call — and you describe it as just keeping things tidy.
cells.ask: Name one thing you did this week that was actually a fairness call and tell someone it was one. Not why. Just that it was.
cells.core:
The instrument is running and you're not claiming it. You make small calls about what's owed, what's right, where the line is — and when it comes up you say something neutral, like it was obvious, like it was just how things are done. The work is happening. The name isn't on it.

The practice is what carried it this far. All those repetitions built a read that lands without argument now, and it works fine — it's the credit that's missing. What's underneath is simpler than the version you tell. Not a rule you follow. Just a direct read of what's fair, accurate enough to be trusted without a defense.
cells.sheetLine: The calls are already yours. You haven't said so.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person's private fairness-sense is currently active and trustworthy — the record supports a mechanism, not a verdict on their particular life. A reader could reasonably say the fairness-sense is distorted or weaponized rather than simply mis-seated. The asks survive being wrong because they are small visible acts (write it down, let the tally stand, one rep, one sentence) that teach something regardless. The sentence that serves me more than them is any clean, certain line about 'knowing what's right' — it sounds wise and tells them nothing they can use. Fixed: no verdicts, no 'you are a fair person', every claim tied to what the capacity is doing in a moment they could recognize.
